Publishing is the [command-line render](run-locally.html), run on a GitHub
runner and pushed to the IG repository's `gh-pages` branch. There is no
separate recipe: the workflow runs the same `stage-local.ts` command that
you run by hand.

GitHub workflows here are **started by hand** (`workflow_dispatch`). Nothing
publishes on push.

## The publishing pipeline
{: #the-pipeline data-fa-label="sec:publishing-the-pipeline" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/fhir-harness/edit/main/docs/source/fhir-publishing/the-pipeline.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/fhir-publishing/the-pipeline.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/fhir-publishing/the-pipeline.md" data-repo="litlfred/fhir-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="the-pipeline.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/fhir-harness/fhir-publishing/the-pipeline.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/fhir-harness/fhir-publishing/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="the-pipeline.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/fhir-harness/fhir-publishing/the-pipeline.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/fhir-harness/fhir-publishing/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

```
input/, sushi-config.yaml, ig.ini
   │  ig-ast-refresh.yml      (reusable; the only writer of the AST cache)
   ▼
cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id>    the AST cache branch
   │  site-publish.yml → stage-local.ts   (no Publisher runs here)
   ▼
gh-pages:  /                   from the default branch
           /branches/<branch>/ from any other branch (a preview)
   │  GitHub Pages
   ▼
https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/
```

| Workflow | Where it lives | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`ig-ast-refresh.yml`](https://github.com/litlfred/fhir-harness/blob/main/.github/workflows/ig-ast-refresh.yml) | this layer (reusable, `workflow_call`) | restores the cache and judges it (`valid`, `stale`, `cannot-tell` or `missing`). If it is not valid, it builds the AST: incrementally when it can, in full otherwise. It seeds the cache branch only from a default-branch commit; otherwise it uploads the AST as an `output-ast` run artifact |
| [`templates/ig-repo-site/ig-ast-refresh.yml`](https://github.com/litlfred/fhir-harness/blob/main/templates/ig-repo-site/ig-ast-refresh.yml) | copied into the IG repository | the caller. A layer above adds its own `pre-export:` step and `template-repos:` here |
| [`templates/ig-repo-site/site-publish.yml`](https://github.com/litlfred/fhir-harness/blob/main/templates/ig-repo-site/site-publish.yml) | copied into the IG repository, unchanged | job `ast` calls the refresh. Job `publish` mounts the layers from `index.lock.json` and runs `stage-local.ts --repo .`; the `plan` input adds `--plan` |
| [`publish-qa.yml`](https://github.com/litlfred/fhir-harness/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish-qa.yml) | this layer | publishes this layer's QA results to `cat/cat-harness/qa-reports` |

The rules (when an AST is valid, who may seed the cache, what a stale AST
refuses) are in the `ig-build-pipeline` skill, §"The AST cache lifecycle".

## Where each output lands
{: #where-it-lands data-fa-label="sec:publishing-where-it-lands" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/fhir-harness/edit/main/docs/source/fhir-publishing/where-it-lands.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/fhir-publishing/where-it-lands.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/fhir-publishing/where-it-lands.md" data-repo="litlfred/fhir-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="where-it-lands.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/fhir-harness/fhir-publishing/where-it-lands.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/fhir-harness/fhir-publishing/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="where-it-lands.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/fhir-harness/fhir-publishing/where-it-lands.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/fhir-harness/fhir-publishing/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

| Output | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| the site | `gh-pages` root | the default-branch publish replaces the root and keeps `branches/` and `_render-log/` (and anything else the IG lists in `site.build.keep`) |
| a preview | `gh-pages:branches/<branch>/` | carries no binaries |
| the AST | branch `cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id>` | one orphan commit: the AST, `expansions.json` and `txcache/` |
| the artefact index | `<site>/fhir-artifact-index/` | `index.json`, `menu.json`, `ig-identity.json`, `releases.json`, and `package.tgz` |
| per-artefact data | `<site>/artifact/<Type>-<id>.{html,jsonld,json}`, `<site>/ast-data/`, `<site>/<Type>-<id>.json` | the thin pages load these |
| build stamp | `<site>/folio-build.json` | which commit and toolchain built the site |
| release binaries | GitHub **release assets** | `package.tgz`, `full-ig.zip` and the like are never put on `gh-pages`; `releases.json` records each asset's URL and SHA-256 |

Why binaries stay off `gh-pages`: GitHub Pages serves at most 1 GB. On one
measured IG, 966.5 MB of its `gh-pages` was Publisher binaries copied into
branch previews. See the `ig-binary-artefacts` skill.

This layer itself publishes:

- **These pages**, on the platform's documentation site:
  <https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/fhir-harness/>.
- **Its JSON-LD context**, which every node it writes points at:
  <https://litlfred.github.io/fhir-harness/ns/context/v1.jsonld>.
- **The reusable workflow and the templates**, from the repository:
  [`.github/workflows/`](https://github.com/litlfred/fhir-harness/tree/main/.github/workflows)
  and [`templates/ig-repo-site/`](https://github.com/litlfred/fhir-harness/tree/main/templates/ig-repo-site).

An IG built on this layer publishes at its own repository's Pages address,
`https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/`. Every such site has the same shape:

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `/` | the IG's home page |
| `/artifacts.html`, `/toc.html` | the artefact list and the table of contents |
| `/fhir-artifact-index/index.json` | the artefact index, machine-readable |
| `/artifact/<Type>-<id>.jsonld` | one JSON-LD node per artefact |
| `/folio-build.json` | the build stamp |
| `/branches/<branch>/` | branch previews |

The layers that build particular guides link their live sites from their own
pages.

## Deployment targets: GitHub Pages and Cloudflare
{: #deployment-targets data-fa-label="sec:publishing-deployment-targets" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/fhir-harness/edit/main/docs/source/fhir-publishing/deployment-targets.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/fhir-publishing/deployment-targets.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/fhir-publishing/deployment-targets.md" data-repo="litlfred/fhir-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="deployment-targets.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/fhir-harness/fhir-publishing/deployment-targets.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/fhir-harness/fhir-publishing/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="deployment-targets.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/fhir-harness/fhir-publishing/deployment-targets.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/fhir-harness/fhir-publishing/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

**GitHub Pages is the only target that is built and running.** The
publisher writes the site to `gh-pages`, and GitHub serves it.

The harness declares the targets it allows, so a new one is a declared option
rather than a hidden switch:

- `PUBLICATION_HOSTS` (in cat-harness-tools `schemas/kg/cat-harness.ts`):
  `github-pages`, `local-server`, `jurisdiction-endpoint` or `none`. A missing
  value does **not** default to `github-pages`.
- `ARTIFACT_STORE_KINDS` (in `schemas/sdlc/artifact-store.ts`):
  `github-release`, `object-store` (R2, S3 and similar) or `site-tree`, each
  with `publicBaseUrl`, `immutableUrls` and `cacheTtlSeconds`. A store that is
  not declared is refused; it never falls back to GitHub.
- The `render-kg-to-cdn` skill treats each CDN as its own Tool with its own
  process. Only the GitHub Pages Tool exists today.

| Option | Status for IG sites | How it would work |
|---|---|---|
| **GitHub Pages** | **in use** | `gh-pages` branch → `https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/`. Limits: 1 GB per site, 100 MB per file |
| **GitHub Pages + custom domain** | available, not set up | a `CNAME` file on `gh-pages` and a DNS record. Nothing in the pipeline changes |
| **Cloudflare Pages** | not set up | connect Cloudflare Pages to the IG repository's `gh-pages` branch with no build command, so it serves the same files from Cloudflare's edge. Nothing in the pipeline changes |
| **Cloudflare R2 + CDN** | not set up for IG sites | upload the built site, or only the release binaries, to an R2 bucket as an `object-store` artifact store. This would be a new deploy Tool, run with `wrangler` |

One layer in this checkout already deploys to Cloudflare: the WHO IRIS
mirror's `iris-cdn.yml` puts content-addressed files into R2 and keeps its
release history in a git repository on Cloudflare. It is a model for an R2
target, not an IG deploy.

**Two things carry over to any host.** The site is built for one base URL
(`SITE_BASEURL`, for example `/<repo>`), so serving it from another path, such
as the root of a custom domain, means building it with that base URL, not
copying the files. And Cloudflare Pages caps each deployment's file count (at
the time of writing, 20,000 files on the free plan) and file size (25 MiB).
An IG with many artefacts and languages can pass the cap, so count the files
on `gh-pages` first.

**Before choosing Cloudflare**, decide three things: who holds the API token
(it is a repository secret, never in a file); whether previews (`branches/`)
move too or stay on GitHub; and whether the canonical URL changes. A
canonical URL that moves breaks every link already published.
